newsitem.title: GERMANY: German May industry orders fall, end 4-mth uptrend.
newsitem.headline: German May industry orders fall, end 4-mth uptrend.

text.p: German industrial orders fell by 0.8 percent in May from the previous month, breaking a four-month uptrend which had culminated in a 3.7 percent rise in April, the Economics Ministry said on Thursday.
Despite the slowdown, May industry orders were still 5.9 percent higher than the same month a year earlier, a smaller gain than the 7.0 percent rise posted in April.
A Reuters survey of analysts had shown that, on average, they expected a monthly fall in May orders of 0.6 percent and a year-on-year rise of 6.2 percent.

West German industrial orders were down by a monthly 1.1 percent in May after a 3.7 percent rise in April. In eastern Germany, orders maintained their rising trend to gain by 3.8 percent after jumping by 4.7 percent.
The Economics Ministry said that the fall in May arose because a series of big industrial orders between January and April was not sustained into the latest month.

On a two-month comparison of April and May against the same period in 1996, industry orders were up by 6.9 percent, with foreign orders leading the way with a rise of 12.5 percent and domestic orders rising more slowly at 3.5 percent.

The industry orders data follows the release of industry production numbers on Wednesday which showed a monthly fall of 0.2 percent -- the first drop since January. Excluding weak mining and construction output, however, manufacturing showed a more encouraging rise of 0.5 percent.
